newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HudCon pulls out of Docklands Stadium bid.
newsitem.headline: HudCon pulls out of Docklands Stadium bid.

text.p: Australian property group Hudson Conway Ltd has pulled out of a bid consortium vying for the right to build Melbourne's Docklands Stadium project.
The Docklands Authority, which will choose the winning bid, said on Thursday that Hudson Conway had exited the bid, leaving its partner, Lend Lease Corp Ltd, as a sole bidder.
"Hudson Conway has advised the authority it will not participate further in the bid for the stadium at Melbourne Docklands," the authority said.
The 52,0000-seat stadium is to be built as part of the Docklands development of Melbourne city's waterfront.
The stadium is estimated to cost between A$200 million and A$300 million. The entire Docklands redevelopment is estimated to cost around A$2 billion.
Hudson Conway was not immediately available for comment.
The authority said Hudson Conway remained involved in the Melbourne Docklands consortium bidding for the right to redevelop the entire five docklands precincts.
The consortium also includes Lend Lease and Mirvac Ltd .
